target.title: fix #95279: Provide a trusted inbound-decoration contract so consumers can strip/dedup without forgeable text heuristics
target.body:
Fixes #95279

## What Problem This Solves

- **Affected surface / workflow:** Inbound user turns that OpenClaw decorates with model-facing metadata, plus the transcript readers that later render, replay, index, dedupe, or summarize those turns: Control UI chat text, CLI imported-session history, memory-host session corpus, LLM historical replay, and session usage logs.
- **Root cause, in product terms:** The root cause was a missing trusted source-of-truth contract for decorated inbound bodies: host-generated inbound metadata and user-authored text were stored in the same `content` string, so downstream consumers had to parse forgeable plaintext sentinels such as `Conversation info (untrusted metadata):` or `Sender (untrusted metadata):`. Because the parser/normalizer could not distinguish host decoration from literal user text, metadata-shaped user text could be stripped or deduped incorrectly.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** Users who paste or type metadata-looking text should not lose that text from chat history, imported-history dedupe, session logs, memory export, or historical replay when OpenClaw has a trusted bare body for the inbound turn.
- **Fix classification:** Root-cause fix for a compatibility-sensitive session-state and data-format contract bug.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Complete shipped solution:** This PR adds an additive trusted inbound contract: persisted/runtime user messages can carry `inboundDecorated: true` plus `bareBody`, and inbound template context can carry `InboundDecorated` plus `BareBody`. Consumers prefer the trusted bare body when the marker is present, then fall back to legacy sentinel stripping for old unmarked transcripts.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** This fixes the source contract instead of adding another sentinel parser. The resolver treats `bareBody` as authoritative only when the trusted inbound marker is present, and the updated readers share that resolver so display, replay, indexing, dedupe, memory, and usage logs all map decorated messages from the same non-forgeable contract rather than independently parsing user-controlled text.
- **Key design boundary / source of truth:** The source of truth is the trusted inbound metadata on the message or inbound context, not sentinel text in `content`. Active-turn model prompts may still contain inbound metadata; historical display, replay, indexing, dedupe, memory, and usage-log readers consume the trusted bare body when present.
- **Non-goals / what did not change:** Scope boundary: this PR only adds and consumes the trusted inbound bare-body contract. It does not change active-turn prompt construction, does not remove legacy stripping for already-persisted rows, does not migrate transcript files, does not redesign plugin SDKs, and does not add unrelated provider/channel routing behavior.
- **Compatibility, merge-risk, or maintainer-decision notes:** Existing unmarked transcripts keep their current legacy fallback. Marked transcripts get one trusted interpretation across the updated readers. The proof now includes focused regression tests plus an exact-head recorder-backed runtime proof that persists a decorated user turn through the shared transcript writer and reads it back through the real reader functions; external channel/gateway proof remains unavailable in this local environment and is disclosed below.
- **Risk labels considered:** `message-delivery`, `security-boundary`, `session-state`.
- **Risk explanation:** Consumers now trust `bareBody` only when `inboundDecorated === true` or `InboundDecorated === true`. A redaction hook that rewrites or mutates user `content` drops the prior trusted fields unless the hook explicitly supplies fresh trusted fields, preventing redacted content from being bypassed by stale bare-body metadata.
- **Why acceptable:** The contract is optional and backward-compatible. It narrows behavior by replacing text heuristics with a trusted marker while keeping legacy fallback for old rows. The test suite covers the reader paths most likely to drop or dedupe user-authored text.

## User Impact

- **Users/operators/developers can now:** Preserve literal inbound-metadata-looking user text through UI display/extraction, CLI import dedupe, memory-host export, LLM historical replay, and session usage logs when a decorated inbound turn carries a trusted bare body.
- **Existing behavior preserved:** Old transcripts without the trusted marker still use `stripInboundMetadata()` and related legacy cleanup, so existing stored sessions remain readable and do not need migration.
- **What was not tested or remains unavailable:** External live gateway/channel proof remains unavailable in this local Windows/Git Bash environment because the prework check reports no local gateway proof capability for the reviewer-requested live channel run. The submitted proof is current-head repository runtime proof plus regression proof over transcript/UI/CLI/runtime/memory/session-log boundaries using a real temp session transcript and synthetic message data; it now includes the hook-redaction boundary requested by review. Earlier broader checks also noted SonarLint was unavailable, `pnpm check:changed` was blocked by a launcher sanity check, and a full non-incremental `tsc` run exhausted local Node heap; focused Vitest, tsgo, oxlint, diff checks, and the exact-head runtime proof listed below passed in the repaired worktree.

## Evidence

- **Environment:** Local Windows/Git Bash worktree, existing PR repair flow, repository Vitest runner, repository tsgo and oxlint runners from earlier repair rounds, and daily-fix verification bound to the current synced repair head `1561111bdc254ae9b96f0c4ade8991bf4ddc0b77`.
- **Commands run after this patch:** `git diff --check`; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts`; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts ui/src/lib/chat/message-extract.test.ts ui/src/lib/chat/message-normalizer.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.llm-boundary.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts`; `node --import tsx --input-type=module` with a recorder-backed exact-head proof importing `createUserTurnTranscriptRecorder`, `loadSessionLogs`, `buildSessionEntry`, and `normalizeMessage`. Earlier repair rounds also passed the focused trusted-inbound suite, core tsgo, core-test tsgo, oxlint shards, and a reader-only exact-head runtime proof after sync and conflict repair.
- **Key results / observations:** All current-head commands listed above exited 0. The session usage log regression proves both compatibility paths: an unmarked decorated legacy row strips injected metadata to `hello there`, while a marked decorated row preserves a literal `Conversation info (untrusted metadata):` string from trusted `bareBody`. The current-head recorder-backed proof ran on `1561111bdc254ae9b96f0c4ade8991bf4ddc0b77`, used `createUserTurnTranscriptRecorder` to persist decorated user turns through the shared transcript writer before reading them back, and observed: transcript writer persisted `inboundDecorated: true`; transcript writer persisted trusted `bareBody`; usage logs legacy row `hello there`; usage logs trusted row `"Conversation info (untrusted metadata):\nthis is literal user text from the trusted recorder path"`; memory corpus includes the trusted literal user text; memory corpus omits the decorated transport body; UI normalization returns the trusted literal body; an in-place `before_message_write` redaction clears the trusted marker; in-place redaction clears `bareBody`; usage logs show only `"[redacted in place by hook]"`; memory corpus omits the redacted bare body; UI normalization shows only the redacted row. After syncing the repair branch onto current main to clear the remote merge conflict, `daily_fix.sh check-main-drift` previously reported only two newer main commits, `sync_main_required=false`, `has_conflicts=false`, and no overlap files, so no further rebase was needed before this proof/commit.
- **Review findings addressed, if any:** RF-001 fixed by capturing the original content before `before_message_write` runs, so spread-return and in-place hook rewrites both clear stale trusted `bareBody`/`inboundDecorated`; proof: `src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts` plus the recorder-backed runtime proof. RF-002 fixed by rerunning exact-head session proof after the redaction fix on `1561111bdc254ae9b96f0c4ade8991bf4ddc0b77` with only synthetic identifiers and no keys/endpoints/user data. RF-003 fixed to the local runtime extent by the recorder-backed proof that covers trusted-body preservation and hook-redaction clearing in one realistic session writer/readback path; external live gateway/channel proof remains unavailable and disclosed. RF-004 fixed by the redaction-boundary code change that compares post-hook content to the pre-hook content snapshot and clears trusted fields after any rewrite. RF-005 is a maintainer-decision item: this PR proposes the trusted inbound contract as top-level `inboundDecorated` plus `bareBody` fields, and maintainers should accept that shape or redirect it under an OpenClaw-owned metadata slot before merge. RF-006 fixed by the exact-head recorder-backed proof that covers trusted body and hook boundary in the shared session transcript writer path. RF-007 partially fixed and partially external: the redaction leak is fixed and proved locally, while durable field-shape acceptance remains maintainer-owned and contributor live setup proof remains unavailable here. RF-008 fixed by clearing trusted bodies after in-place hook rewrites. RF-009 fixed by the added in-place mutation regression in `src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts`. RF-010 fixed by running `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts` successfully. RF-011 fixed to the local runtime extent by the recorder-backed proof showing literal metadata-looking user text is preserved and redacted hook content cannot leak through trusted bare-body metadata. RF-012 was a non-blocking maintainer pass signal with no requested code change.
- **Regression guardrail:** Target test files: `src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts` and `src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts`. The session transcript regression now covers a `before_message_write` hook that mutates `event.message.content` in place and verifies `bareBody`/`inboundDecorated` are cleared. The session usage log regression locks in both compatibility paths: one unmarked legacy decorated user row must still strip injected metadata, while one trusted decorated user row must preserve a literal `Conversation info (untrusted metadata):` string from `bareBody`. The broader focused test suite also covers transcript persistence and redaction, inbound context sanitization, CLI imported-history dedupe, UI extraction/normalization, memory-host session export, media-only inbound transcript expectations, and LLM-boundary historical replay.
- **Patch quality notes:** Patch quality warnings were reviewed. The resolver uses defensive message-like reads only at existing union/runtime boundaries where persisted rows, inbound template context, and UI-normalized messages do not share one static schema; those type escapes are guarded by explicit boolean/string checks and default to legacy behavior or `undefined`/`null`, not to silently trusting content. The session-files retry/catch is test-only Windows teardown cleanup and does not mask assertion failures. Default returns in the LLM-boundary and UI normalizer are narrow guards for absent trusted metadata. The larger diff is intentional because the contract must be written once and consumed at every affected display/replay/indexing/dedupe/log boundary; the latest merge-conflict resolution preserves current-main sender metadata under `__openclaw` while also preserving this PR's `inboundDecorated` and `bareBody` fields.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for the local code paths covered by regression proof and current-head recorder-backed runtime proof. The only remaining caveats are the disclosed external live gateway/channel proof gap in this environment and maintainer acceptance of the durable field shape.

## Real behavior proof

- **Current-head redacted runtime transcript:** This PR now includes current-head real behavior proof on `1561111bdc254ae9b96f0c4ade8991bf4ddc0b77`. The proof was run outside Vitest with `node --import tsx --input-type=module`; it imported `createUserTurnTranscriptRecorder`, persisted decorated inbound user turns through the shared transcript writer, then read the generated transcript back through `loadSessionLogs`, `buildSessionEntry`, and `normalizeMessage`. It also persisted an in-place hook-redacted turn to prove stale trusted fields are cleared after hook mutation.

```text
$ git rev-parse HEAD
1561111bdc254ae9b96f0c4ade8991bf4ddc0b77

$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <recorder-backed exact-head runtime proof with in-place hook redaction>
Recorder-backed exact-head runtime proof: PASS
HEAD: 1561111bdc254ae9b96f0c4ade8991bf4ddc0b77
transcript writer persisted trusted marker: true
transcript writer persisted bare body: "Conversation info (untrusted metadata):\nthis is literal user text from the trusted recorder path"
usage logs legacy row: hello there
usage logs trusted row: "Conversation info (untrusted metadata):\nthis is literal user text from the trusted recorder path"
memory corpus trusted row: "User: Conversation info (untrusted metadata): this is literal user text from the trusted recorder path"
memory corpus omits decorated transport copy: true
UI normalized trusted row: "Conversation info (untrusted metadata):\nthis is literal user text from the trusted recorder path"
in-place hook redaction clears trusted marker: true
in-place hook redaction clears bare body: true
usage logs redacted row: "[redacted in place by hook]"
memory corpus omits redacted bare body: true
UI normalized redacted row: "[redacted in place by hook]"
transcript file: temporary session JSONL created by createUserTurnTranscriptRecorder
EXIT_CODE=0
```

- **What this proves beyond tests:** The recorder-backed proof exercises the real transcript writer seam and the same real reader functions that production reader paths use after transcript persistence: the shared recorder persists the trusted marker and bare body, session usage logs strip legacy injected metadata, trusted decorated session rows preserve literal metadata-looking user text, memory-host indexing uses the trusted bare body instead of the decorated transport copy, UI normalization returns the trusted literal body, and an in-place hook redaction cannot leak the stale trusted bare body through usage logs, memory, or UI normalization.
- **Boundary of this proof:** This is a local session recorder and reader runtime proof from the repaired worktree, not a live external gateway/channel proof. It avoids model/provider dispatch and does not require API credentials. The local environment could not provide the requested live gateway/channel proof capability, so that gap remains disclosed for maintainer or ClawSweeper judgment.

## Implementation summary

- Add optional trusted inbound fields on persisted/runtime user messages and inbound template context.
- Persist the trusted bare body for decorated user turns while treating `before_message_write` as the redaction boundary.
- Update UI display, UI text extraction/search/export, CLI imported-session dedupe, memory-host session indexing, LLM historical replay, and session usage logs to prefer the trusted bare body before legacy sentinel stripping.
- Keep legacy sentinel stripping for old transcripts that do not carry trusted fields.

## Scope boundary

In scope: inbound user-turn contract/type plumbing, transcript persistence/runtime merge preservation, UI display normalization, CLI imported-session dedupe, memory-host session export/indexing, LLM historical replay normalization, session usage logs, and regression tests for those paths.

Out of scope: transcript migration, removal of legacy fallback, active-turn model prompt construction changes, unrelated provider/channel routing, or broad plugin SDK redesign.

## Related PR scan

The daily-fix related open PR scan found related PR #94419 as advisory background only. This PR does not depend on that work and keeps the fix scoped to the trusted inbound bare-body contract requested by #95279.

## Verification history

Additional local validation from earlier repair rounds also passed after sync/rebase repair:

```text
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo
# exit=0

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test.tsbuildinfo
# exit=0

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts ui/src/lib/chat/message-extract.test.ts ui/src/lib/chat/message-normalizer.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.llm-boundary.test.ts
# exit=0

node scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mjs --threads=8
# exit=0
```

## Merge risk

- Risk labels considered: `message-delivery`, `security-boundary`, `session-state`.
- Risk explanation: This changes display/replay/indexing/dedupe/log behavior for messages that explicitly opt into the trusted decorated contract. The security boundary is the trusted marker plus redaction-hook clearing behavior. Session-state risk is additive because old rows retain legacy sentinel stripping.
- Why acceptable: The contract is optional and backward-compatible, and the tests cover the affected boundaries.
